questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(1,0,-2)$, $B(1,2,4)$, and $C(3,-2,1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨1,0,-2⟩,\,b=⟨1,2,4⟩,\,c=⟨3,-2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨1,2,4⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,2,6⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨3,-2,1⟩-⟨1,0,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{0\cdot 2+2\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 3}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{3}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{40}\cdot \sqrt{17}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{170}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{7}{\sqrt{170}})≈{58}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}p=⟨0,4,5⟩,\,q=⟨1,5,4⟩,\,r=⟨2,3,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨1,5,4⟩-⟨0,4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨2,3,6⟩-⟨0,4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0)={90}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Consider the points $A(5,3t+2,2),$ $B(1,3t,2)$ and $C(1,4t,3).$ Find $∠ABC$ given that $\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}=4.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨5,\,3t+2,\,2⟩,\,b=⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩,\,c=⟨1,\,4t,\,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠ABC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/2c81d48afacc4ac5e81ab501bc713009ea4425451fcf8dbf414672aeadbb1679.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA} & =a-b \\  & =⟨5,\,3t+2,\,2⟩-⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,2,\,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{BC} & =c-b \\  & =⟨1,\,4t,\,3⟩-⟨1,\,3t,\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}=4$, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC} & =4 \\ 4\cdot 0+2\cdot t+0\cdot 1 & =4 \\ 0+2t+0 & =4 \\ 2t & =4 \\ t & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{BA} & =⟨4,2,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{BC} & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{BA}$ and $\overset{\to }{BC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{BA}\cdot \overset{\to }{BC}}{|\overset{\to }{BA}||\overset{\to }{BC}|} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{20}\cdot \sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{100}} \\  & =\frac{4}{10} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{5})≈{66.42}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given the Value of Their Dot Product
questions.problem: Consider the points $A(2t,-1,5)$, $B(-3,t,1)$ and $C(2t+1,2,-t).$ Find $∠BAC$ given that $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=5.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩,\,b=⟨-3,\,t,\,1⟩,\,c=⟨2t+1,\,2,\,-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨-3,\,t,\,1⟩-⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3-2t,\,t+1,\,-4⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨2t+1,\,2,\,-t⟩-⟨2t,\,-1,\,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,3,\,-t-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=5$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =5 \\ (-3-2t)\cdot 1+(t+1)\cdot 3+-4\cdot (-t-5) & =5 \\ -3-2t+3t+3+4t+20 & =5 \\ 5t+20 & =5 \\ 5t & =-15 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨-3-2(-3),(-3)+1,-4⟩, \\  & =⟨3,-2,-4⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =1,\,3,\,-(-3)-5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-4)^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{29}\cdot \sqrt{14}} \\  & =\frac{5}{\sqrt{406}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{5}{\sqrt{406}})≈{75.63}^{∘}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Angle Between Two Vectors Given Three Points
questions.problem: Find $∠BAC$ given the points $A(2,-1,2)$, $B(3,-5,1)$, and $C(1,-4,-1).$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,-1,2⟩,\,b=⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,c=⟨1,-4,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3,-5,1⟩-⟨2,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-4,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨1,-4,-1⟩-⟨2,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-1)+(-4)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot (-3)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{18}\cdot \sqrt{19}} \\  & =\frac{14}{3\sqrt{38}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{14}{3\sqrt{38}})≈{41}^{∘}.
$$
